text: Functions: parts, return values, order, and reusable helpers.
dist(...) body runs
parameters in → return value out

A function packs a computation under a name. Calling it jumps into the body with the arguments copied into the parameters, runs until return , and hands back one value. You write the logic once and test it once.
Parts: return type, name, parameter list, body. A function that returns nothing has type void . A function must be declared above the code that calls it.
Piece In dist.cpp return type double name dist parameters double x1, double y1, … body the lines between { } return return sqrt(...); ends the call call dist(x1, y1, x2, y2) in an expression
Write the three side lengths once as a function instead of copying the formula three times (P5735). One fix in the function fixes every call.
Calling a function that is defined below main without a declaration (prototype) above gives "was not declared in this scope". Either put helpers above main , or declare them first.
A non-void function must return on every path. Falling off the end returns garbage, and the compiler only warns.
A lambda, [](int x) { return x * x * x; } , is a small unnamed function written where it is used. You met one as the comparison in sort .
Small yes/no and number helpers make the main loop read like the statement.

A bool helper can return as soon as the answer is known: return false inside the loop stops the whole function. vector<int> is a C++ array that grows with push_back and knows its size() ; handy when you do not know the count in advance (P5736, P5737).
Once isPrime exists, "write each even number as a sum of two primes, smallest first" is just two loops and one test. The helper hides the details, so the main loop reads like the statement (P1304).
Reuse helpers across problems: the same isPrime solves P5736, P1304, P1217 and P1075. Keep a tested copy in your notes.
Averages after dropping the highest and lowest score fit one function, double judge(int a[], int m) , called once per singer (P5738).

title: 变量作用域与参数传递

text: Copies or references, arrays as parameters, and where a name lives.
by value: int x
a (main)
x (copy) by reference: int &x
a = x (same box) x = 100 changes only the copy, or the original itself
By default a parameter is a copy: changing it inside the function does not touch the caller's variable. Add & to make it a reference, another name for the caller's variable, so changes stick.
Use & to change arguments (swap) or to send back several results. Use const string &s to pass a big object without copying it and without changing it.
An array argument is never copied: the function works on the caller's array, so changes are visible outside. Pass the length n along with it. Write const when the function should only read.

Kind Lives Starts as global (outside all functions) whole program 0 local (inside { }) until its block ends garbage unless set parameter during the call the argument value static local whole program, one copy 0, set once
A local with the same name as a global hides it. Give globals clear names; ::cnt reaches the global one when you must.
Base case, smaller call, call stack, and memoisation.
fact(3) = 3 × fact(2) fact(2) = 2 × fact(1) fact(1) = 1 (base) calls results return upward: 1 → 2 → 6

Every recursive function has a base case that answers directly, and a recursive case that calls itself on a smaller input and combines the result. Each call waits on a stack until the call it made returns.
No base case, or a step that does not shrink the input, means infinite recursion: the program crashes with a stack overflow. Very deep recursion (around 105–106 levels) can crash too.
fact(3) fact(2) fact(1)

Recursion fits when the answer for n is built from the answer for a smaller n: factorial (P5739), working backwards day by day (P5743). Any such recursion can also be written as a loop; recursion is shorter, the loop avoids deep stacks.

title: Divide into parts: a recursive picture

text: Split the square into four quarters: one is handled directly, the other three are the same problem at half size. The function only describes one level; recursion repeats it down to size 1 (P5461).
Plain fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2) recomputes the same values again and again: about 2n calls, hopeless for n = 50.
Store each result the first time it is computed and return it straight away next time. Now each fib(k) is computed once: O(n). This "remember results" idea is the seed of dynamic programming.
Some answers need no recursion at all: the sum over all subsets of a set is (sum of elements) × 2n−1, because each element appears in half of the subsets (P2415).
Group fields, member functions, arrays of structs, and sorting them.
Student s s.name "senpai" s.chinese 114 s.math 51 s.english 4 s.total() 169
A struct is a new type made of named fields. One Student carries a name and three scores together, so sorting or picking the best student moves the whole record at once.

Access fields with a dot: s.name . A struct can also hold functions (member functions) that use its fields, such as s.total() . An array of structs, Student a[1005] , is a table with one row per student.
senpai 114 51 4
senpai 114 51 4
senpai 100 80 91
fafa lxl lxl senpai

Using > (not >= ) when searching for the best keeps the first student among ties (P5740). The pair loop from 入门 4 works unchanged on structs (P5741). Student &s = a[best] gives a short name for one record without copying it.
kkksc03 24 0 chen_zhe 14 400
kkksc03 25 0 chen_zhe 15 480
Pass a struct by reference (Person &p ) when the function should update it; by const Person &p when it only reads. Passing by value copies every field.

score * 1.2 uses floating point and can land just below the true value. score * 6 / 5 stays exact in integers (P5744). Compute weighted scores such as 70% + 30% the same way, as 7 * a + 3 * b compared with 10 * limit (P5742).
Tell sort what "comes first" means.
bob 240 amy 240 cat 300 dan 180
cat 300 amy 240 bob 240 dan 180
sort(a, a + n, cmp) calls cmp(x, y) to ask "must x come before y?". Compare the main key first; only when it ties, compare the next key.
cmp must be a strict order: return false when x and y are equal. Writing >= instead of > can crash sort .
Alternative: give the struct an operator< and call plain sort(a, a + n) . For one-off orders a lambda works too: sort(a, a + n, [](const Student &x, const Student &y) { return x.score > y.score; }) .

C C LANGUAGE · ADDITIONAL INFORMATION C has no references. To change the caller's variable, C passes its address with &x and the function works through a pointer with * . C++ code still meets this in older solutions.
A C struct has no member functions, and in C you must write struct Student s; (or use typedef ). Sorting in C uses qsort with a comparison that returns a negative, zero or positive int .
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. A function = return type, name, parameters, body; void returns nothing.
2. Define or declare a function above the code that calls it.
3. Every path of a non-void function must return a value.
4. Parameters are copies; add & to change the caller's variable or return several results.
5. Pass big objects as const T &; arrays are never copied, so pass n too.
6. Locals start as garbage and hide globals of the same name.
7. Write tested helpers once: isPrime, isLeap, gcd; return as soon as the answer is known.
8. Recursion = base case + a call on a smaller input; no base case → stack overflow.
9. Recomputed recursion (fib) is exponential; memoise results to make it linear.
10. A struct groups fields; access with s.field; member functions like s.total().
11. Best record: compare with > to keep the first among ties.
12. Sort structs with cmp(x, y) = "x before y": main key first, then tie-breaks; never >=.
13. Keep scores exact: score * 6 / 5, not score * 1.2.
14. (C) C passes pointers (&x, *p) instead of references, and sorts with qsort.
